title: A connected étale finite-Tor lisse complex has one perfect constant value
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Use the small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $L\in D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\underline R)$ has bounded cohomology, each $H^q(L)$ is locally constant with finitely generated $R$-module values [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^q(L\otimes_R^L F)=0$ for every degree-zero étale $R$-module sheaf $F$ and $q
otin[a,b]$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Then there is a perfect ring complex $E\in D(R)$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] and an étale covering $\{V_i	o X\}$ with $L|_{V_i}\simeq\underline E|_{V_i}$. For every geometric point $ ar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], $E\simeq L_{ ar x}$.

Moreover, if $W	o X$ is an affine object of the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] that is weakly contractible (evaluation at $W$ takes every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection) [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible], then $(
u_X^*L)|_W\simeq\underline E|_W$, where $
u_X$ is the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Neither $R$ nor its finitely generated modules are required to be finite sets.

source.place: Tag 09BI, lemma-connected-ctf-locally-constant; the weakly contractible corollary is the trivialization used in proetale.tex, proof of Tag 09C6, together with the covering-splitting condition of sites.tex Tag 090K.

proof.text: Take a K-flat flat-term representative P of L. The constant ring sheaf in degree zero is K-flat (tensoring with it is the identity); the derived-tensor model identifies L\otimes_R^L\underline R with P\otimes_R\underline R\cong P, by x\otimes r\mapsto rx and inverse x\mapsto x\otimes1. Taking F=\underline R therefore gives H^q(L)=0 off [a,b]. Apply the existing bounded-constant-model lemma on the small étale site: obtain a covering {V_i\to X} and complexes M_i^\bullet of finitely generated R-modules, zero outside [a,b], with L|_{V_i}\simeq\underline{M_i^\bullet}. Discard empty V_i. On a nonempty V_i\times_XV_j choose a geometric point; exact geometric stalks, and the constant-sheaf stalk isomorphism termwise, give M_i^\bullet\simeq M_j^\bullet in D(R). These isomorphisms are R-linear since the constant-stalk maps commute with every scalar endomorphism. If the images of V_i and V_j meet, choose a geometric point above a point of intersection and lifts to both étale schemes; the more precise clause of the cited geometric-lifting lemma gives lifts above the chosen points of both fibres. Thus their fibre product is nonempty. For each derived-isomorphism class M among the M_i, form the union of the images of its V_i. These unions are open by the cited openness theorem, are pairwise disjoint by the overlap argument, and cover X. Nonemptiness and connectedness imply exactly one class occurs. Choose its representative M^\bullet. Each geometric point of X lifts to some V_i, so the same exact-stalk calculation gives M^\bullet\simeq L_{\bar x} for every geometric point \bar x.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point \bar x of X (one exists because X is nonempty). Its stalk is the inverse image of the topos point p supplied by the cited topos-point lemma. The constant-stalk isomorphism identifies p^{-1}\underline R with R, so module pullback along p is precisely the exact stalk functor, and Lp^*=p^*. For an arbitrary R-module N in degree zero, apply the Tor hypothesis with F=\underline N. The derived tensor/pullback comparison and the constant-stalk isomorphism give p^*(L\otimes_R^L\underline N)\simeq L_{\bar x}\otimes_R^L N\simeq M^\bullet\otimes_R^L N. Exactness of the stalk functor commutes with cohomology, hence this object vanishes in cohomology off [a,b]. Thus the bounded finite-module complex M^\bullet has Tor amplitude [a,b]. The cited bounded-finite-Tor-perfect theorem gives a complex E of finitely generated projective R-modules, zero outside [a,b], isomorphic to M^\bullet in D(R). Termwise constant presheaves preserve exact sequences, and the cited module sheafification theorem is exact; consequently constant-sheaf construction preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces a functor on derived categories. Applying it to E\simeq M^\bullet gives L|_{V_i}\simeq\underline E|_{V_i}. Step 1 also gives E\simeq L_{\bar x} for every geometric point.

proof.text:
Let W	o X be affine and weakly contractible. The geometric comparison inverse image preserves constant sheaves: the constant sheaf of a set is the sheaf coproduct of that many copies of the terminal object; inverse image preserves these coproducts and the terminal object. Preservation of finite products identifies the ring and module operations as well, for arbitrary R. The cited classical-module comparison supplies exactness on R-module sheaves, so it acts termwise on derived categories. Next, 
u^* commutes with restriction to each étale V_i. Write u:V_i	o X. For an object T	o V_i of (V_i)_{proét}, the indexing category of the pro-étale inverse-image colimit at T has the initial object (T	o X,(\mathrm{str},\mathrm{id}_T):T	o V_i	imes_XT): a map from it to (V,\varphi) must be \mathrm{pr}_2\varphi, because a map into V_i	imes_XV over V_i is determined by its second component. So the presheaf inverse image along u is F\mapsto F(T	o X), which is already a sheaf by the weakly-étale localization lemma; hence u_{proét}^{-1} is restriction to X_{proét}/V_i\simeq(V_i)_{proét}. The same initial-object argument identifies u_{ét}^{-1} with restriction to X_{ét}/V_i, which the étale localization lemma identifies with (V_i)_{ét}. The cited comparison-pullback isomorphism 
u_{V_i}^*u_{ét}^{-1}\simeq u_{proét}^{-1}
u_X^* therefore gives (
u_X^*G)|_{V_i}\simeq
u_{V_i}^*(G|_{V_i}), natural in the sheaf G. By naturality it respects addition and every scalar endomorphism, so it is an isomorphism of module sheaves, and it is exact. Apply it termwise, then use relocalization along W	imes_XV_i	o V_i. Step 2 then gives (
u_X^*L)|_{W	imes_XV_i}\simeq\underline E there. The projections W	imes_XV_i	o W are étale and jointly surjective by the cited covering base-change lemma. As W is affine, the refinement lemma gives a finite affine refinement {U_j	o W}. Each U_j still has this local isomorphism, by exact restriction and the constant-restriction isomorphism. Let U=\coprod_{j=1}^m U_j, with q:U	o W. The scheme-coproduct lemma makes its summands pairwise disjoint and clopen. U is affine, being a finite coproduct of affines. So q is an étale map of affine schemes, given by an étale ring map. That map is ind-étale (a constant filtered colimit), hence weakly étale by the ind-étale stability lemma. Its composite with the weakly étale W	o X is weakly étale by the composition lemma, so U is an object of X_proét over W, as in the localization lemma. The covering {U_j	o W} gives an epimorphism h_U	o h_W: any map T	o W lifts after the covering {T	imes_WU_j	o T}. The pro-étale topology is subcanonical, so weak contractibility gives a sheaf section h_W	o h_U and Yoneda identifies it with a scheme map s:W	o U satisfying q\circ s=id_W.

proof.text: Combine the finitely many isomorphisms on U_j to an isomorphism (\nu_X^*L)|_U\simeq\underline E|_U as follows. For any object T\to U, put T_j=T\times_UU_j. The T_j are disjoint and cover T, so the sheaf condition is F(T)=\prod_{j=1}^m F(T_j); no overlap compatibility remains because all distinct intersections are empty and a module sheaf on the empty object is zero. This identifies module sheaves on the slice over U with the finite product of their categories on the slices over U_j, with restriction and inverse assembly exact. Apply the identification termwise to complexes: differentials, chain maps, homotopies and cohomology are computed on each component. In particular the finite family of roofs representing the local derived isomorphisms assembles to a roof on U, and its quasi-isomorphism legs remain quasi-isomorphisms componentwise. Now restrict this isomorphism along s:W\to U, using exact derived restriction and its relocalization identity. Since q\circ s=id_W, its left-hand object becomes (\nu_X^*L)|_W; constant-restriction naturality identifies the right-hand object with \underline E|_W. This proves the moreover clause, including disconnected W. If W is empty both restrictions are zero, and the same conclusion holds.
